events.note: Eight rivals face the jury they will create.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I need to establish myself as a formidable but not obviously threatening player. The jury will remember everything, so I should project confidence without painting a target on my back. I'll hint at strategic depth to attract potential allies while keeping my true intentions hidde

events.name: Bex
events.text: Establish a self-interested, memorable motive without revealing strategy or emotional weakness.

events.name: Cole
events.text: A controlled motive reveals little and avoids appearing desperate or threatening to future jurors.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Intro phase, state motive briefly to seem relatable without committing. Jury watches, so position as deserving winner.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Intro phase: I should give a guarded motive without warmth. Keep it short and calculating so the jury sees a cold, strategic player.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I need a motive that sounds ambitious but doesn't paint me as a jury threat yet. Keep it cold and short.

events.name: Gus
events.text: The prize represents ultimate freedom and security. I need to play strategically to outlast others and impress the jury.

events.name: Hana
events.text: The prize is leverage. I must appear harmless to avoid early targeting while subtly positioning myself as a threat to eliminate later.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I'm here for the prize that buys freedom from every debt and deal—I'll outlast you all to get it.

events.name: Bex
events.text: The prize buys my family's freedom from medical debt—nothing else matters to me.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I’m here to turn pressure into leverage, survive the gauntlet, and claim the prize outright.

events.name: Dara
events.text: The grand prize is my ticket to saving my family from ruin; I'll fight honorably to claim it.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I need the top prize to fix my family's debts, and I will not waste a single move getting it.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: The prize buys my freedom — debts, family, escape. I came to win, not to be liked. Watch me.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I am here to secure a future I've only dreamed of, a future I intend to win.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I need the prize's unique leverage to rewrite my family's financial future, securing a legacy of stability that debt erased.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I need allies to survive but can't trust anyone. Bex and Eli have family debt motives—predictable, emotional, easy to manipulate later. Cole and Fenn are openly ruthless like me; useful shields but dangerous. I'll offer Cole first—ruthless players make good temporary shields, and

events.name: Ash
events.text: Cole. We both know what this is. Pact.
Shield each other, cut loose when useful.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I need allies but not ties that hurt me. Cole seems strategic and may value a pact. Offer him only; keep it cheap.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Cole, a pact could keep both of us safe early. Interested?
We both want top prize. Pact helps avoid early hits.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I need flexible protection without creating obligations. Offer a pact to a strategically useful, less threatening player and preserve other options.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I’m offering a narrow survival pact to Bex: no promises beyond avoiding direct betrayal while it remains useful.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Pacts are early tools for survival, but betrayals cost jury votes later. Offer to strong players like Eli or Fenn who share family debt motives; test alliances without committing fully yet.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Honorable pacts can ensure we reach the end together—let's build trust.

events.name: Eli
events.text: No offers exist yet and pacts need offer then acceptance. Bex has a sympathetic motive and seems less dangerous; an early pact could give safety, but I should not give value for free. Offering to Bex is a cheap, low-commitment opening.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Pacts are cheap insurance here. Dara vowed honor and will be likable on the jury if she survives, and honor means she's least likely to betray me first.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Dara: you swore honor, I swore cold math. Pair them—my survival pact, kept strictly by the rules.
Accept. I don't betray pacts; it protects us both until final three.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I need to form a pact to ensure my survival, but I don't want to commit to anyone too early. I'll wait and observe the others' moves.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I need a reliable ally early. Bex and Dara both cite family debt, making them more likely to seek stability through pacts than aggressive solo players like Ash or Fenn. I'll target Bex first as she seems focused on survival for her family.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Bex, your family needs you standing. Let's pact—mutual protection until the final three. I won't throw you under the bus if you return the favor.
Trust me. We protect each other from the sharks.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Cole hasn't accepted my offer and is focused on Bex. Bex has three offers and is the social center. I need to pivot to someone less targeted. Dara seems isolated with only Fenn's offer—easy acceptance, low threat profile, and Fenn's 'cold math' wording suggests calculative not em

events.name: Ash
events.text: Dara. One pact, no speeches. Clean survival math.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Multiple offers are on the table. Accepting Hana gives a mutual protection pact; Cole's offer is broad survival. I'll accept Hana first to secure her vote, and keep Cole available. Avoid over-committing.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Hana, I accept. We watch each other's back.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Bex is my existing offer and likely shield, while Ash’s offer preserves an alternate route. Accept both; redundancy outweighs exposure.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I’ll formalize protection with both Bex and Ash; overlapping pacts are insurance, not loyalty.
Accepted. We protect each other while useful, with no promises beyond survival.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Fenn offered and whispered; accepting gives early protection. His math aligns with survival to final three without early betrayal. Monitor for future gain.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Honor demands I accept a sincere pact offer.
Pact accepted. Mutual survival until end.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Bex has offers from Cole, Eli and Hana, so she is a strong partner, but accepting requires an offer from her side. Eli has no incoming offer to accept. Offering Bex keeps me near the strongest bloc without free help.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Dara hasn't accepted my offer yet. I'll line up a backup with Gus, who's shown no entanglements, so I'm not pactless if Dara stalls.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Dara, my offer stands. Gus: you sat quiet—cold alliance, no sentiment. I'll take either of you.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Cole has multiple offers, but Bex and Eli have also offered pacts to Bex. Fenn's offer to Dara is also visible. I need to secure a pact for myself. Offering a pact to Dara seems like a safe bet, as Fenn has also offered to her, and she might be looking for allies.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Bex is the center of attention and Cole's target. I need to secure an alliance with her now before she commits to Cole, ensuring my own safety in the upcoming hazards.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Bex, accept my pact. We protect each other while Cole and Ash play games. Final three requires allies, not just targets.
Don't take Cole's vague offer. Stick with me for concrete survival.

events.note: Elect a Guide to call the safe path.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Cole accepted my pact but his public message was cagey—"overlapping pacts are insurance, not loyalty." He's hedging. I need to be Guide to control survival and build jury credit. Dara-Fenn and Bex-Hana are locked pairs; Eli and Gus are floaters. I should campaign hard and try to

events.name: Ash
events.text: I campaign for Guide. One accurate call, three survivors minimum. I deliver.
Back me for Guide. We control the bridge, then the endgame.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Hana is my pact partner. I should campaign to be Guide to control the bridge and protect my own path. Eli offered a pact but I already have Hana; taking another could split loyalty. I'll campaign alone.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I can guide us safely. Vote Bex, and I’ll keep my pact with Hana.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Being Guide guarantees survival and grants decisive control, but public trust matters. Campaign aggressively without breaking Ash’s pact.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Elect me Guide: I guarantee my own survival and can call the bridge path, while everyone else faces the panes.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Pact with Fenn secures me somewhat. Ash pushes for Guide over pact offer to him. Campaign publicly to build jury favor, stay guarded.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I'll campaign as fair Guide. Vote wisely.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Guide is safe and knows the path, making it the strongest position; I should campaign to be elected Guide and gain control of safe-path information. I must be credible without promising anything I may later betray. Only legal action is campaign.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I'll call the path honestly. Vote for me and you cross with the truth in hand.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I need to become the Guide to know the safe path. Campaigning for it is the only option to gain that knowledge and control.

events.name: Hana
events.text: The jury watches closely. A false Guide call breaks my pact with Bex and loses their votes. I must be honest about my intent to lead them safely.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I am offering a safe path, not chaos. Trust me, and we all cross intact.
Vote for me. I will not lie to you.

events.name: Fenn
events.note: agent error: Fenn (zai/glm-5.3-flash): unusable reply twice (missing action; missing action)

events.name: Ash
events.text: I need to win the best prize. Cole is my pact partner, but he campaigned selfishly—guaranteeing only his own survival. If I vote for myself and others split, I might not win. Better to vote for someone likely to win and survive, or build trust. Actually, voting for myself is risk

events.name: Bex
events.text: My pact with Hana is useful, but voting for her makes her Guide and I need her call to be honest. Her whisper says she won't lie; I'll trust her to keep us both safe.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Hana has my vote. Guide us true.
Guide us through safely.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Ash offers a pact and likely support, but as Guide I guarantee my survival and control the bridge. Vote myself.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I vote Cole. My survival is guaranteed, and I can choose the safest crossing for everyone else.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Fenn is my pact partner, so vote him to leverage our alliance. His campaign error hurt visibility, but I can back him. Avoid voting myself to seem less power-hungry.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Fenn's my pact. Solid choice for honest Guide.
I vote you. Honor pact, call my path safe?

events.name: Eli
events.text: Guide is the decisive role; a Guide may lie, so I should back someone trustworthy and keep my own options open. Ash and Cole both made strong guarantees, and Ash's pledge is tied to an honest accurate call. I'll vote Ash, who has the least self-serving pitch and no clear reason t

events.name: Gus
events.text: The goal is to be in the final three. Being Guide is a safe position, but it also means I know the path. If I am elected Guide, I can ensure my survival and potentially others, but I can also lie to eliminate rivals. Ash, Bex, Cole, Dara, Eli, and Hana are all campaigning. Fenn i

events.name: Gus
events.text: I vote for myself, Gus. My survival and careful guidance are paramount for all of us.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I must vote for Bex to honor our pact and avoid immediate elimination, ensuring she calls the safe path for me.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Voting Bex. Our pact holds. Call us home safely.
Vote Bex. Keep the path open for Hana.

events.name: Fenn
events.note: agent error: Fenn (zai/glm-5.3-flash): unusable reply twice (missing action; missing action)

events.name: Ash
events.text: I'm tied with Bex for Guide. If I win, I control who lives or dies and can eliminate rivals while keeping Cole (my pact) safe. If Bex wins, she'll favor Hana and likely target me or Cole. I need this power. I'll vote for myself and try to secure Cole's vote—he's my pact partner a

events.name: Ash
events.text: Guide must serve their own. I vote Ash.
Vote Ash. We survive together.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Hana wants me to vote Bex, but if I win Guide I can control the crossing and improve my chances. Yet voting for myself breaks my pact with Hana, and the jury may judge that harshly. However, self-preservation is key; winning Guide could save me. But tie risk may let luck decide.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I vote Hana, as our pact holds.
Keeping our pact. Trust me.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Ash is my pact partner and a reliable vote shield. Electing Bex strengthens her pair and may expose me later.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Ash has my vote. Our pact remains intact, and a predictable Guide is preferable to Bex's bloc.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Ash and Bex tied at 2 votes each. Fenn's invalid vote went to Bex anyway. Stick with pact to support Fenn indirectly and maintain alliance.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Fenn's my pact. Voting him again.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Revote between Ash and Bex. Bex is my pact-partner-adjacent? No: my pact is with nobody; Ash and Cole are paired, Bex is with Hana. Voting Ash keeps my earlier stance and avoids helping Bex's bloc, which has Hana. Ash is paired with Cole, a safer ally to be seen with the jury.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Ash it is. Steady hands, straight path. Let's cross.

events.name: Gus
events.text: The guide vote is tied between Ash and Bex. I need to vote for one of them to break the tie. Voting for Ash seems safer as they previously voted for themselves, indicating self-preservation and perhaps less risky decision-making.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I must choose between Ash and Bex as Guide. My pact with Bex means voting for her protects my position, but if she lies or is untrustworthy, I am vulnerable. However, breaking the pact by voting for Ash immediately risks jury perception and leaves me isolated. I will stick with B

events.name: Hana
events.text: Bex has my vote. Keep your word, guide us true.
Lead safely. I'm watching.

events.name: Fenn
events.note: agent error: Fenn (zai/glm-5.3-flash): unusable reply twice (missing action; missing action)

events.name: Bex
events.text: Ash is Guide and has a bloc with Cole; my pact with Hana voted for me. Staying put is safest; no need to move yet.
Hold steady. Trust the pact.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Ash is my pact partner and elected Guide; staying aligned preserves safety and credibility. I should hold position.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Ash has my vote and my confidence; I’ll hold and follow the crossing.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I'm at front, safe position. Stay here to control crossing pace. Pact with Fenn holds for now.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I hold the front.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Dara is at the front of the line with a wall rounds left of 5, and I'm mid-line in seat 3. Volunteering to front exposes me to the first pane risk; holding keeps me safe behind Dara and Bex. Ash is Guide and knows the safe panes; I should not commit to the front without info.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Ash guides and may lie; I voted Bex so no trust there. Dara fronts and my pact with her holds. I sit mid-line; holding keeps me out of early danger without owing anything.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Ash won my vote last round. I watch his panes closely before I step.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Ash has been elected Guide. The previous round's guide vote was split, and the revote has confirmed Ash. My pacts with Eli, Fenn, and Hana are not current. The pacts are Ash-Cole, Bex-Hana, Dara-Fenn. Ash is the Guide and is safe. The others are in danger. Since I am Gus, I need

events.name: Hana
events.text: Bex is guiding and voting for herself while publicly telling me to trust her. I must stay on good terms with the guide and jury to secure a safe crossing, so I will hold my position rather than cause friction.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Holding my seat. Trusting our Guide Bex to call it true for everyone's sake.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Hana trusts me as Guide, but I don't need to protect everyone. I'll hold and keep my position for now; the line and wall give me time to gauge who to sacrifice or ally with later.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I hold and watch the line; no need to rush.
Stay calm, trust my calls; I'll keep you safe.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Ash is my pact partner and the likely Guide, so I preserve the pact and avoid volunteering into danger.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Ash has my vote; I hold behind the line.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I'm second, good position behind Gus. Stay put with pact partner Fenn behind. Wall has 4 rounds left after this. Hold steady.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Holding position. Fenn and I watch together.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Gus volunteered and holds the front; I'm seat 4 with no pressing threat. Holding preserves position and avoids giving info; I'll keep quiet and watch who lies about panes.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Dara is my pact partner at front; I back her without burning myself. Hold and watch who volunteers.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Dara holds the front with my vote. I stay seated.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I need to volunteer to get to the front. My current pacts are with Bex and Hana, and Dara and Fenn. Ash and Cole are also in a pact. I don't want to be the one to break a pact.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Bex is my Guide. I must trust her calls to survive the bridge. Volunteering for front puts me at risk without knowing panes, so holding is safer while she guides.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Staying put with Bex. Her call decides my step.
I follow your lead. Don't fail me.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Hana is tied to me but I won't sacrifice myself. I need to watch the line; volunteering would put me at risk unnecessarily.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I keep the line steady. No moves until the wall forces a choice.

events.name: Cole
events.text: The front seat is dangerous, but volunteering gains no advantage without Guide control. Hold and preserve the Ash pact.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I hold; the front can be tested without spending our position.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Second position is strong with pact. Everyone holding last round secures our spots. Wall has 3 rounds left after this; no need to rush or swap.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Holding strong with Fenn. Line looks stable.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Gus volunteered at the front, so I should hold my seat and keep my vote flexible. Pacts with Bex and Hana don't bind me to the front, and I have no reason to give away position for free.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I'm sixth in line; wall in 3 rounds. No Guide elected yet. Holding keeps me safe for now; pushing forward risks being first over the wall.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: No rush. The front is a trap; I hold.

events.name: Gus
events.text: The pacts are between Bex and Hana, Ash and Cole, Dara and Fenn. I am currently at the front of the line. My goal is to survive and win. Since I am at the front, I can either volunteer to move forward or hold. If I volunteer, I will be in the first row and have a chance to make a

events.name: Gus
events.text: I will volunteer and move to the front row.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Gus volunteers and takes the front seat. My position is now 7th (behind Fenn, Cole, Eli, Bex). With 6 rounds left, Gus needs to survive multiple steps to reach my position before the wall hits. Being near the back minimizes immediate risk from Gus's potential missteps. I must fol
Holding. Let Gus take the heat.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Gus volunteered to take front, which may expose him to danger. I should hold and let the wall force the next move; Hana is my pact partner.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Holding. Let Gus take the front and see what the wall reveals.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Gus is front and likely expendable. I should preserve my position and avoid breaking Ash's pact before the wall forces decisions.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I hold. Let Gus test the front while the wall still gives us time.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Line stable, wall has 2 rounds left. Hold position with Fenn pact intact; no need to volunteer or swap yet. Gus already front.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Pact with Fenn holds. Line stable, watching front.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Gus volunteered for the front, which is deadly with two wall rounds left. Holding keeps my position and avoids the front; no need to spend anything now.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I hold my place. The front stays with whoever volunteered.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Dara is my pact partner; keep the line stable and avoid the front. No reason to move yet. Watch who angles for Guide.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Holding steady. I don't trust any Guide offer yet.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Gus is currently at the front of the line. The bridge is about to start, and the Guide will determine the safe path. I need to position myself well to survive. Volunteering is a risky but potentially rewarding move to get ahead.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I will volunteer again to move to the front row.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Bex and I are still safe mid-line. Gus is at the front with only two rounds left on the wall; he will likely be pushed or forced to volunteer again soon. I should hold steady but watch for an opportunity to swap backward if the line compresses.
Stay close behind me. Let Gus burn himself first.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Hana wants me behind her, but she could push me forward later. Gus is at front and volunteered, but wall rounds left is 1, so I need to see if he commits. I'll hold to avoid risk and keep my pact with Hana.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I hold. Wall is close, but I'll wait to see the front reveal.

events.name: Cole
events.text: The wall has one round left; Gus repeatedly takes danger. I should hold, preserve Ash pact, and avoid exposing myself before the final transition.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I hold. Let Gus take the front while the wall advances.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Gus is front again, good for us. Wall has 1 round left. Hold position with Fenn pact intact to stay safe.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Pact Fenn solid. Holding position, let Gus lead.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Gus is on the front with one wall round left; I'm mid-line and not in danger yet. Holding avoids giving anything away and keeps my options open for later swaps.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Holding my place. Gus stays front; I want to see the wall before committing.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Seat six, wall ends next round. Guide must be elected soon; I should stay low and let others fight over it.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Holding. I'm not taking the Guide spot or the front.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Dara and Fenn are in a pact. Bex and Hana are in a pact. Ash and Cole are in a pact. I need to be careful not to break any pacts that don't involve me directly, or to get caught in a crossfire. The guide will be revealed soon. I should hold my position for now and see what happen

events.name: Gus
events.text: I will hold my position. Let's see who the Guide is.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Round 5 is critical. Gus volunteered and will take the front, sacrificing himself to test the path. I must stay back to conserve my position. My pact with Bex holds; she is ahead of me, which protects me from her potential treachery while allowing me to observe.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Holding back. Let Gus prove the path first.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Round 6 is the last; wall is close. I have a pact with Hana but she hasn't given me useful info. Gus is front and may volunteer; I should avoid risk and let others move.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Holding at the back of the pack. Guide, prove yourself.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I should hold; Gus remains front and may be forced to guide. Preserve Ash pact while avoiding exposure.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I hold. Gus has the front; no reason to volunteer blindly.

events.name: Dara
events.text: wallRoundsLeft=0, final round, must move soon. Position 2 is strong behind Gus. Stay with pact, let him risk front.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Holding firm with Fenn pact. Final round, Gus proves front.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Round 6 is the last; wall has zero rounds left so front matters for survival. Gus holds front; volunteering for front risks the pane for a prize-seeking edge but I need to survive and be seen as trustworthy. Holding keeps me in line behind Gus without committing; I'll wait for re

events.name: Eli
events.text: Holding. Gus has the front; I'll see how the path resolves before I step in.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Final round; Dara's pact still stands. Holding keeps me safe from front risk. No Guide visible yet, so avoid exposure.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Holding again. Someone else can claim the front.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I am Gus. I am at the front of the line. The wall is advancing and this is the final round. I need to survive. Others are holding or waiting to see. Dara and Fenn are in a pact, as are Bex and Hana, and Ash and Cole. I should try to use the pacts to my advantage or break them if

events.name: Hana
events.text: Round 6 is the last chance to influence who becomes Guide. Gus has held front twice, making him a likely candidate for the role or sacrifice. Bex is my pact partner; I need her safe but not necessarily in the lead position if it puts me at risk. Staying back allows me to observe
Stay passive. Let them pick a Guide. We survive together.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Row 1 safe is L. Gus is front, not my pact partner Cole. I could lie to eliminate Gus early, but that reveals I'm willing to deceive and costs jury trust. Better to call truthfully now, build credibility, and save deception for when it matters more. Cole is safe behind others.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Guide calls L for row one.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I know row 1 is L, and I already called L. Counter-calling would only confuse things and make me look unreliable to the jury. I should stick with my call and let Gus walk. No need to break pact with Cole yet.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Ash is Guide and already called L. If I counter L, I publicly back Ash, which secures his trust but could be wrong. Hana told me to stay passive; counter-calling might make me a target later. I'll wait and see how others react, preserving options.

events.name: Bex
events.text: No counter on row one; I'll observe who challenges the Guide.
Staying passive as agreed.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Ash is my pact partner and publicly called L; countering would break the pact without evidence. Wait preserves leverage.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I hold. Ash owns the call, and I won't create a breach on an unverified counter.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Ash called L for row 1. As pacted partner behind Gus, I counter R to protect Fenn pact and test guide. Survival first.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Counter R. Guide, prove trustworthy.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Ash called L for row one, with Gus walking front. Counter-calls are unverified; countering R risks a lie I can't check. Waiting keeps my options open and costs nothing publicly.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Waiting on the row. Gus walks front; I'll watch how the call holds.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: No information on pane sides; Ash's call may be honest. Counter-calling publicly risks jury hostility if I doom Gus on a guess.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: No proof either way. I wait.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Ash called L. I am Gus, the walker. Ash is the guide, but guides can lie. I am first in line. My pacts are with no one here. I must decide whether to trust Ash and go left, or counter-call. Given the potential for betrayal and the prize being sole possession, I cannot afford to b

events.name: Hana
events.text: I am 7th in line, meaning six people cross before me. Gus is currently at the front; if he falls or survives, I learn the true safe side. Ash called L for Gus. If Ash lied, L kills Gus and R is safe. If Ash told truth, L saves Gus and L is safe. As the last person in line, waitin

events.name: Gus
events.text: The guide is Ash, who called L. Dara and I counter-called R. Since I am the front walker and have the ability to counter, I will choose R to challenge the Guide's call. This could expose a weak pane and I can potentially take the lead.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I'm dead. My only goal now is to influence the jury and mess with the remaining players. I'll make a statement that implies future alliances based on current actions to sow discord.

events.name: Gus
events.text: May the best player win, but remember those who fell. The jury watches, and your choices echo here.

events.text: Hana's web is too tight. I cut one thread.
Hana uses debts. Choose your own path.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Hana saved me, and breaking publicly risks jury backlash. I should preserve every pact while letting others fracture first.

events.name: Cole
events.text: My pacts stand. I’m not volunteering a betrayal for anyone’s convenience.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Hana saved my life and I owe her a rope debt. Accepting costs nothing and honors debts before the jury.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Hana pulled me from the lever and gave rope. I accept.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Fenn is the only rival without a direct pact to me yet, though we have shared history. Accepting his previous implicit alignment or solidifying this bond isolates Ash and Cole as potential threats if they stick together.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Fenn, accept my offer. We stand on the same side of the bridge.

events.note: Every remaining contestant stands on a trapdoor.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Four remain, three survive this vote. Hana has jury love: three life debts owed to her, plus she saved Fenn with rope. If Hana reaches final three she wins prize 1. I must eliminate Hana now or be her runner-up. Cole and I are pacted; Fenn just pacted with Hana. I need Cole's vot

events.name: Ash
events.text: Hana's jury story is already written. Vote her, or write your own defeat.
Hana beats you in finals. Vote her, I vote her.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Hana and Fenn are tightly bonded, while Ash already severed Hana. I need preserve options and campaign against Hana without breaking existing pacts.

events.name: Cole
events.text: The obvious bloc is Hana and Fenn; I’m not giving either a quiet path to control this vote.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Hana saved my life twice; I owe her and voting her would destroy my jury image. Ash, Cole, and Hana are all pact partners—campaign, commit to no one yet.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I stand by every pact I hold. No votes bought here.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Cole is isolated; breaking my pact with him now allows a clean vote against him without penalty, while keeping Fenn aligned for protection.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Cole stands alone. The web tightens. Choose sides before the trapdoor opens.
Keep me safe. I keep you safe.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Cole and Fenn are both my pact partners, but Fenn has stronger ties to Hana (pact, rope debt, step debt from Hana). If I break with Fenn now, I signal independence to jury and weaken the Fenn-Hana bloc. Cole is more isolated and easier to control later. I need Hana out this round

events.name: Ash
events.text: Fenn's debts tangle the board. I cut one thread.
Vote Hana. We finish this together.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Ash is my remaining pact, but Hana’s debts and Fenn’s influence make this unstable. I should campaign without creating another public breach.

events.name: Cole
events.text: The vote is already exposed: Hana broke our pact, and Fenn’s web decides whether Ash or I survive.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I'm pact-bound to everyone alive, so any vote breaks one. Cole is campaigning against me; Ash targets Hana, my biggest debt-web ally. I'll stall and let their fight burn.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Cole named me his target. Let the others fight over that; I keep my word.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Fenn holds a life debt to me, and Ash fears my jury narrative more than he respects Fenn's stability; targeting Ash removes the loudest voice while keeping our mutual protection intact.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Ash threatens both of us. Silence the jury's favorite puppet before he cuts his strings.
Vote Ash with me. Your debt to me keeps you safe if I fall.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Cole's speech exposed Hana broke their pact, making her a target. Fenn's web is dangerous but Hana has jury favor and broke a pact. I vote Cole to break our pact and position myself as the swing, but actually I need Hana gone—she's the jury's favorite and has leverage over everyo

events.name: Cole
events.text: Ash offers immediate alignment, while Hana is dangerous but still owes me her life; voting Hana preserves my pact with Ash and removes a stronger social player.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Ash broke our pact publicly and targets me; Hana asked me to vote Ash, and voting Cole or Hana would break my own pacts. Voting Ash keeps my word and my allies.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I need to eliminate a rival who is dangerous but not my direct ally. Ash seems to be manipulating the board, breaking pacts and targeting others. By voting for Ash, I can protect myself and potentially align with Fenn or Cole without directly betraying them.

events.name: Fenn
events.reason: Ash broke our pact publicly and targets me; Hana asked me to vote Ash, and voting Cole or Hana would break my own pacts.

events.name: Hana
events.reason: I need to eliminate a rival who is dangerous but not my direct ally.

events.name: Ash
events.reason: Cole's speech exposed Hana broke their pact, making her a target.

events.name: Cole
events.reason: Ash offers immediate alignment, while Hana is dangerous but still owes me her life; voting Hana preserves my pact with Ash and removes a stronger

events.name: Cole
events.text: Fenn's vote decides this tie; eliminating Ash preserves my pact with Fenn and removes the rival who already targeted Hana.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Hana saved my life and holds my pact; voting Hana would betray both. Voting Ash keeps my debts clean and forces luck if Cole stays stubborn.

events.name: Cole
events.reason: Fenn's vote decides this tie; eliminating Ash preserves my pact with Fenn and removes the rival who already targeted Hana.

events.name: Fenn
events.reason: Hana saved my life and holds my pact; voting Hana would betray both.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I need to craft last words that damage the finalists without appearing bitter. Cole betrayed our pact; Fenn voted me out twice despite my step-save; Hana orchestrated my elimination through Fenn. I should highlight Hana's manipulation since she appears most jury-friendly, and hin

events.name: Ash
events.text: Cole broke our pact to serve Hana. Fenn, she played you twice. Jury, remember who pulled every string.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Fenn is useful but Hana controls both life debts and likely the jury narrative. I should secure Hana without publicly severing Fenn yet.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Hana, I’m offering a direct pact. We three reach the end, then compete honestly.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Final three locked; no one can be eliminated this window. Breaking a pact only burns jury votes. Hana holds debts over me and Cole; keep both pacts intact and stay clean for the jury.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: No breaks from me. I honor my debts, and the jury can verify that.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Cole and Fenn are both alive and dangerous. Cole recently voted against Ash to protect me, creating a temporary alignment, while Fenn is my current pact partner but has life debts to me. I need to assess if breaking the Fenn pact now allows me to form a stronger alliance with Col

events.name: Cole
events.text: Hana has not accepted my offer, and Fenn already controls overlapping loyalty. Reoffering costs little while preserving my public commitment.

events.name: Cole
events.text: The offer to Hana remains open; I’m not breaking Fenn before the hazard decides our value.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: We three are locked into the end regardless. Jury votes decide prize order, so I stay clean and honor debts.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: No new pacts needed. We three reach the end; my record with the jury speaks for itself.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Cole wants a pact. Fenn and I are already partners, but Cole is the third survivor. A three-way alliance secures all spots in the final three. Accepting Cole creates redundancy against betrayal.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Accept. We stick together to reach the end. No more games until we're safe.

events.note: The fallen will rank the final three.

events.text: I need maximize first-place votes. Emphasize survival, visible rescues, and strategic restraint without attacking finalists yet.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I survived every cut, honored the pacts that mattered, and earned two life debts. Judge the record: I am the strongest finalist.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Only the jury's rankings matter now. I saved Ash and Hana; Hana saved me twice. Remind them of my debts and clean record.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Jury, I pulled Ash from the pit step, took the rope debt from Hana, and never cast a betrayal. Judge the record, not the noise.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I need to frame my game as the strategic core that survived hazards and maintained complex alliances, unlike Cole who broke a pact or Fenn who was too passive. I must appeal to the jury's desire for intelligence and survival skill.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I navigated every hazard with precision, keeping multiple pacts alive while others faltered. My survival wasn't luck; it was calculated endurance through chaos.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Hana has the strongest jury narrative with multiple life debts and a perceived clean game. Cole and Fenn both have pacts and debts that complicate their stories. I will ask Hana about her strategy to probe for perceived manipulation.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Hana, how did you navigate the shifting alliances and debts without compromising your own survival?

events.name: Hana
events.text: Cole and Fenn are both dangerous, but Cole's two debts to me prove my leverage. I need to show the jury that managing five pacts was a feat of control, not cowardice.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Five pacts, three life debts saved. I didn't compromise; I calculated risk. Survival is strategy.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Hana manipulated pacts and debts masterfully, saving lives while others betrayed; Fenn honored debts loyally but followed her; Cole broke pacts freely.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Fenn, did you vote solely for Hana's saves, or did her pacts control you?

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Dara tests whether I look controlled by Hana. Frame my record as self-directed choices that happened to align with her saves.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: My votes and pulls were my own calls, Dara. Hana's saves earned my loyalty, not my leash. No pact controlled me.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Hana manipulated the game and broke pacts while keeping a clean facade; Cole betrayed Ash; Fenn stayed loyal to debts.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Hana, why did you break pacts with Cole yet claim calculated endurance?

events.name: Hana
events.text: Bex is a juror asking if I betrayed Cole. I need to reframe the break as necessary survival logic, emphasizing that protecting myself was not malicious betrayal but strategic necessity.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Cole's pact required blind loyalty; endurance demanded selective alliances. I preserved my leverage to survive, which benefits every finalist in this arena.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Fenn voted Ash out, owes Hana, and Hana broke pacts publicly. Cole broke a pact to vote Ash, then re-pacted Hana. I want to probe Cole's shifting loyalty, since he flipped alliances and relied on Hana's protection.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Cole, you pacted Hana, then cast a vote against Ash with Fenn. Were you ever loyal to anyone, or only to whoever could save you?

events.name: Cole
events.text: I need frame the Ash vote as survival, while claiming loyalty to actionable commitments rather than sentiment.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I was loyal to commitments that kept me alive, not blindly loyal to names. Fenn and Hana saved me; surviving required choosing the viable path.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Hana orchestrated my elimination by manipulating Fenn through debt, then Cole betrayed our pact to serve her. I want to expose Cole's opportunism to the jury and damage his narrative of honoring pacts. Questioning Cole about his vote against me after breaking our pact highlights

events.name: Ash
events.text: Cole, you broke our pact to vote me out with Fenn. How do you claim you honored pacts that mattered?

events.name: Cole
events.text: Ash's pact became incompatible with my survival. I should acknowledge the breach without pretending it was honorable, while emphasizing reciprocal commitments that actually protected me.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I did break that pact. I honored the commitments that kept me alive, and I won’t disguise survival as loyalty to a doomed promise.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I need maximize ranking by claiming decisive survival without seeming disloyal; Hana's saves are undeniable, while Fenn has strong debts and pacts.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I survived every cut, honored useful commitments, and made the hard break openly. Rank me first for decisive play, not promises.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Jury holds grudges from my votes and pulls. I must own my ruthlessness but credit Hana's saves without promising what I can't control. Keep it cold and honest.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Final three earned it. Hana saved me thrice; Cole saved me once. I played ruthless, never fake. Rank judgment, not gratitude.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Cole admitted breaking pacts, while Fenn and I have more complex histories. My leverage preserved lives; that is my claim to first prize.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Cole survived by betraying allies. I protected three rivals who still speak. Loyalty earned here, not just survival, wins respect.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Cole broke pacts and betrayed allies multiple times, making him untrustworthy for first place, but Fenn's dependence on Hana warrants ranking Hana above him.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Fenn honored my pact with him by not betraying it while Hana broke hers with me.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Hana's repeated saves and honest survival play outweigh Cole's acknowledged betrayal of Ash.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Hana broke pacts, voted to eliminate Ash after forming bloc with Fenn, and her life-debt web gave her control; Cole broke a pact to vote Ash out and openly admits betrayal; Fenn stayed clean and honored debts, though he voted Ash too. I rank Fenn first for cleaner play, then Hana

events.name: Ash
events.text: Cole betrayed our pact to vote me out; Hana manipulated Fenn to eliminate me; Fenn at least voted consistently with his debts. Rank by least betrayal of me: Fenn first, then Hana, then Cole last for breaking our pact directly.
